clue.text: I am 'Sir' with opera in production

definitions.text: I am 'Sir' with opera in production

parts.note: contracted to I'M

indicators.note: the words are being worked up into a new staging, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knighted showman introduces himself while mounting an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M comes from 'I am'; the letters of SIR and OPERA are reshuffled to give PRESARIO. The whole clue also describes the speaker: a theatrical producer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is the manager who organises and stages operas and concerts.

clue.text: Dished out pocketed snotrag — cheers!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take the snotrag into their pocket, so they go around it
dished means ruined or messed up, so the letters of 'out' are jumbled

parts.note: slang for a handkerchief, a hanky

explanation.surface: Someone hands out a used handkerchief and is thanked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dished' turns OUT into T-OU, which pockets HANKY. 'Snotrag' is jokey British slang for a handkerchief.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Cheers' is informal British thanks, the same as saying thank you.

clue.text: Choice of two awkward cheers (not three in the end)

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters are clumsily rearranged
not says the following letters are left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: the word cheers, taken twice since the clue asks for two of them
the three letters that finish the rearranged string, E and two S's from the plural cheers

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a feeble two cheers rather than the customary three.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the twelve letters of CHEERS CHEERS as RECHERCHE + ESS: 'not three in the end' leaves off those last three letters. The surface plays on the phrase 'two cheers' for half-hearted praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché, borrowed from French, describes something rare, exquisite and carefully selected, i.e. choice.

clue.text: Promise to take edge off blade

indicators.note: an edge is an extremity, so the blade loses its opening letter

parts.note: a sword is a blade

explanation.surface: A vow to blunt a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To give your word is to make a pledge or assurance.

clue.text: If dropped it may start a run, or it may stop one

definitions.text: If dropped it may start a run, or it may stop one

parts.words: If dropped it may start a run, or it may stop one
parts.note: in knitting a lost loop starts a ladder; and a sharp pain in the side halts a runner

explanation.walkthrough: A dropped stitch begins a run (a ladder) in knitting or tights; a stitch, the sudden pain in your side, stops a jogger.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a loop of thread in sewing or knitting and a sharp side cramp from exercise.

clue.text: Crowd round a factory

definitions.meaning: to ... (about or around) is to move about as a crowd
a ... is a factory, as in a cotton ...

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests workers gathering at a works gate; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it describes a throng moving aimlessly; as a noun it is an industrial works.

clue.text: Beloved's likely to be seen within group of angels

indicators.note: the second word shows up inside the first

parts.note: cher is French for dear or beloved; the 's stands for 'has'
apt means likely, as in apt to happen

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is expected to turn up among a host of angels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of angels' sounds heavenly, but it means a local branch of the Hells Angels motorcycle club.
explanation.definitionFit: Hells Angels organise in local branches each called a chapter, so a chapter is one such group of bikers.

clue.text: Dick sticks with garden implement

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue
a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A gardener glues a stick to a hoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' is old slang for a detective (private dick).
explanation.definitionFit: Gumshoe is American slang for a private detective, from their soft quiet shoes.

clue.text: Turn short bit of magic into story with miracles

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a spell is a piece of magic

explanation.surface: A conjuror turns a quick trick into a tale of wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: Each Gospel is a New Testament account of Christ's life, full of miracles.

clue.text: Take millions from the wealthiest? It'll never fly

indicators.note: with 'from', take out the named letter
with 'Take', says the letter comes out of the phrase

parts.note: the most rich
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A tax-the-rich proposal that is dismissed as never getting off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It'll never fly' sounds like a verdict on the policy, but it is a literal description of a flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless bird, so it literally cannot fly.

clue.text: Mangled closed-circuit capturing leak in outhouse

indicators.note: everything before it sits inside the outhouse

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding

indicators.note: the abbreviation holds the leak inside it

parts.note: CC, as in CCTV
to run is to leak, as a tap does

explanation.surface: CCTV in a garden shed catches a leak and the camera is damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrunched means crumpled or crushed, so a scrunched object has been mangled.

clue.text: Flower bud seen around middle of July

indicators.note: the tip goes around the central letters

parts.note: a bud forms at the tip of a shoot, so tip stands for it

indicators.note: the central two letters of July

explanation.surface: A flower bud spotted in midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower bud' reads as one phrase; only 'Flower' defines, and 'bud' is TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring-flowering bulb plant with cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: They try crime writer's sequel to Nine Tailors finally

indicators.note: the writer's name follows the picked letters
the final letter of each of the two words

parts.note: Dorothy L. Sayers, the detective novelist, wrote The Nine Tailors

explanation.surface: A follow-up to Dorothy L. Sayers's novel The Nine Tailors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nine Tailors (1934) is a Lord Peter Wimsey mystery by Sayers, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so essayers are people who make an attempt or try.

clue.text: Expression one sees right through adolescence say

indicators.note: the letter runs through the middle of the stage

parts.note: adolescence is an example of a phase of life

explanation.surface: A wise person seeing straight through a teenager's moods.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a group of words, i.e. an expression or idiom.

clue.text: Send matron fresh dressings

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A request to a hospital matron for clean bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressings' suggests wound bandages; here it means decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Adornments are decorations or trimmings, like the dressings on a shop window.

clue.text: Around pole, tent pitched in sand on vacation became less level

indicators.note: the tent is set up inside the remaining letters
emptied out, leaving only its first and last letters
the tent goes around the letter for pole

parts.note: a teepee is a conical tent
N, the north pole

explanation.surface: Camping on a beach, where the ground slopes around the tent pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that steepened grew more sharply inclined, so it became less flat.

clue.text: Taken to task at the 18?

definitions.meaning: made to answer for one's conduct
18 is LIBRARY; in a library, a volume might literally be carried to a book (shelf)

explanation.walkthrough: 'The 18' refers to the answer at 18-down, LIBRARY, where books are fetched for readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought to book is an idiom for being called to account or punished.

clue.text: Worn out tetra swimming in bottom of lake

indicators.note: the jumbled fish goes inside the lake floor

parts.note: a lake bed

indicators.note: the fish's letters are moving about

explanation.surface: A tired tropical fish swims on the lakebed.
explanation.walkthrough: A tetra is a small tropical aquarium fish; 'swimming' scrambles it, and the floor of a lake is its bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Battered describes something damaged by long use, so it is worn out.

clue.text: A place for 26 and two bits of lingerie underwear on the lines

parts.note: the first two letters of lingerie
a bra is underwear
RY, the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Lingerie items are put on a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is READING; a library is a place for reading. RY = railway, as in lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a building where people go to read books.

clue.text: Landlord's notice to quit perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a notice to quit is an example of a written ...

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the example and the whimsical sense of a person who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a written message and, whimsically, someone who rents out property.

clue.text: When cycling back no ride can be made smooth

indicators.note: letters are moved round from the front to the end
the words are read backwards first

explanation.surface: A cyclist out on a bike would find no ride possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NO RIDE into EDIRON; 'cycling' moves ED from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironed clothes have been pressed so the creases are flattened.

clue.text: Take Crosophile to court after upset? It makes you sick

indicators.note: the turned-round word takes the setter in
the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to summon to court
the setter of this puzzle, so ME

explanation.surface: Someone angry wants to sue the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by pseudonym; Crosophile here is the setter, so ME. 'after upset' reverses the court word, which then takes the setter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that causes vomiting.

clue.text: What criminal gets transported to ends of the known public sphere?

parts.note: sent means transported, recalling convicts shipped to Australia

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A convict shipped off to the far reaches of the known world.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is the punishment imposed on a convicted offender.

clue.text: Poem by Frost for audience

indicators.note: as heard by listeners, so a word with the same sound

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A poem written by Robert Frost read out to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the poet Robert Frost; it is rime, ice crystals.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme is a short verse, as in a nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Yankee facing hearing in 2023 say

indicators.note: set in front of the next piece

parts.note: Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ear is a sense of hearing

explanation.surface: An American attends a court hearing in 2023.
explanation.definitionFit: 2023 is an example of a calendar year.

clue.text: Earlier instance of damage to car by delinquent creep?

indicators.note: placed beside the next piece
badly behaved, so the letters go astray

parts.note: a dent is damage to a car body

explanation.surface: A precedent case where a young thug dented a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is a previous case taken as an example or guide.

clue.text: Call for grand parades, but no soldiers

indicators.note: the soldiers are excluded

parts.note: pageants are spectacular processions
soldier ants, so ants

explanation.surface: A demand for spectacular parades without troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are ANTS, from soldier ants.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to summon them over a loudspeaker or pager.

clue.text: In fear of dropping dead in town

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so the letter for dead falls out of the fearful word

parts.note: dreading means fearing

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of the dead in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a large English town west of London.

clue.text: Who will vote for a change of role etc?

indicators.note: the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Who would vote for a change of job, and so on?
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is a person entitled to cast a vote.
